title: Confronting Abusive Language Online: A Survey from the Ethical and Human Rights Perspective

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying literature that utilizes template-based corpora for professions in language models, measures imbalances in abusive language training datasets, assesses discrepancies between male and female annotators, and decomposes bias along pragmatic and semantic dimensions.

Reviewing literature that evaluates bias through word embedding association tests, measures the skewed representation of vocabulary related to racial demographics in datasets, and analyzes how annotators' dialect unawareness amplifies harms against racial minorities.

Surveying studies that measure higher false positive rates in texts containing markers of African American English (AAE) and assessing how annotator insensitivity to dialects leads to biased ground-truth labels.

Reviewing comprehensive evaluation frameworks including metrics for error disparity across identity groups, true/false positive/negative rate differences for various demographic factors, and Counterfactual Token Fairness (CTF) calculated by swapping identity tokens in utterances.
